question.prompt: If the solutions of the equation \(x^2+px+q=0\) are the cubes of the solutions of the equation \(x^2+mx+n=0,\) then

solutions.explanation:
Let \(r\) and \(s\) be the roots of \(x^2+mx+n=0\), counted with multiplicity. We can use their sum and product without finding the roots individually. Expanding
\[
(x-r)(x-s)=x^2-(r+s)x+rs
\]
and comparing coefficients gives
\[
r+s=-m,\qquad rs=n.
\]
The other quadratic has roots \(r^3\) and \(s^3\), so the same coefficient comparison gives \(r^3+s^3=-p\).

To express this cube sum using quantities we know, factor and then use the square of the sum:
\[
\begin{aligned}
r^3+s^3
&=(r+s)(r^2-rs+s^2)\\
&=(r+s)\bigl((r+s)^2-3rs\bigr)\\
&=(-m)(m^2-3n)\\
&=-m^3+3mn.
\end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(-p=-m^3+3mn\), giving \(\boxed{p=m^3-3mn}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). These identities involve no division by a root or by \(n\), so zero and repeated roots cause no exception.
solutions.title: Express the cube sum using the root sum and product

solutions.explanation:
Let \(r,s\) be the roots of the original quadratic, counted with multiplicity. The expansion
\[
(x-u)(x-v)=x^2-(u+v)x+uv
\]
shows that \(r+s=-m\). Applied to the quadratic with roots \(r^3,s^3\), it also shows that \(r^3+s^3=-p\).

The original equation lets us replace a root's square by a linear expression. For either root \(t\),
\[
t^2=-mt-n.
\]
Multiplying by \(t\) and replacing \(t^2\) again gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
t^3&=-mt^2-nt\\
&=-m(-mt-n)-nt\\
&=(m^2-n)t+mn.
\end{aligned}
\]
Use this formula once for each root and add:
\[
\begin{aligned}
-p=r^3+s^3
&=(m^2-n)(r+s)+2mn\\
&=(m^2-n)(-m)+2mn\\
&=-m^3+3mn.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(\boxed{p=m^3-3mn}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\). No division was used, so the calculation also applies to zero or repeated roots.
